architecture.title: Deltux POS Architecture
architecture.description: An overview of the distributed system architecture behind Deltux POS — designed for availability, multi-tenant isolation and maintainable enterprise integrations.
architecture.layer_presentation_desc: Responsive client application. Handles POS operations, inventory, invoicing, customer management and sales analytics. Deployed on the edge network for low-latency delivery.
architecture.layer_router_tech: SAP Application Router · JWT Validation · Route Config
architecture.layer_router_desc: Routes incoming requests from the frontend to the appropriate backend services. Validates JWT tokens, enforces authorization rules and manages service discovery.
architecture.layer_services_tech: Node.js · SAP CAP · REST APIs · Auth Service
architecture.layer_services_desc: Core business logic services: POS operations, inventory management, invoicing engine, customer/supplier management. Auth Service issues HttpOnly cookies and manages sessions.
architecture.layer_data_desc: Multi-tenant database with row-level security (RLS) ensuring strict data isolation between tenants at the database level — preventing data leaks even under application bugs.
architecture.layer_hint: Click any layer to expand its description
architecture.closing: The architecture separates presentation, routing, business services and persistence, allowing the system to evolve independently while maintaining clear boundaries between responsibilities.
architecture.highlight1_desc: Next.js application optimized for performance. Implements responsive UI with Tailwind CSS and real-time data updates for POS operations.
architecture.highlight2_desc: SAP Application Router manages routing and authorization. Node.js microservices handle business domain logic with clear separation of concerns.
architecture.highlight3_desc: Multi-tenant PostgreSQL with Row-Level Security. Strict data isolation at the database level ensures B2B tenant privacy by design.

challenges.title: Engineering Challenges
challenges.subtitle: Real technical problems encountered during development — and how they were approached.
challenges.deployment_challenge: Managing the deployment of a distributed application composed of frontend, application router and backend services across environments with different configuration dependencies.
challenges.deployment_decision: Use a declarative multi-target deployment model to handle service dependencies and ordering consistently across all environments.
challenges.deployment_solution: Implemented MTA (Multi-Target Application) patterns using mta.yaml for declarative deployments, ensuring correct dependency resolution on Cloud Foundry.
challenges.deployment_outcome: Consistent and repeatable deployments across dev, staging and production environments with automated dependency management.
challenges.auth_challenge: Securely managing user sessions and JWT tokens in a microservices architecture where requests pass through multiple routing layers before reaching backend services.
challenges.auth_decision: Centralize authentication in a dedicated service and propagate identity via internal headers — never exposing tokens to client-side JavaScript.
challenges.auth_solution: Designed a centralized Auth Service that issues HttpOnly, Secure cookies. The Application Router validates tokens and forwards user context via internal headers to downstream services.
challenges.auth_outcome: Secure session management with no token exposure to client-side JavaScript, even when multiple services are involved in the request path.
challenges.isolation_challenge: Ensuring strict data privacy and isolation for B2B tenants in a shared database environment where a single application bug could potentially expose cross-tenant data.
challenges.isolation_decision: Apply security at the database level to prevent any application-layer bypass — making data isolation a guarantee, not a convention.
challenges.isolation_solution: Implemented Row-Level Security (RLS) in PostgreSQL combined with a tenant-aware ORM layer guaranteeing that each query is automatically scoped to the current tenant.
challenges.isolation_outcome: Cross-tenant data leaks impossible at the database level, even under application-level bugs or misconfigured queries.
